attempted_claim: Let d=3 (resp. any fixed d≥3) and (H_{λv,α,φ}u)_n = u_{n-1}+u_{n+1}+λv(φ+nα)u_n on ℓ^2(Z) with v∈C^ω(T^d,R), φ∈T^d, α∈T^d rationally independent, and β(α)=limsup_{k≠0} |k|^{-1} ln(1/‖⟨k,α⟩‖). Does there exist α with β(α)=+∞ such that for every v there is λ_0=λ_0(α,v)>0 with Σ_ac(λv,α) of positive Lebesgue measure for all 0<|λ|<λ_0 and all φ? Decide this existence vs. universal absence in d≥3.
decisive_failure: No proof or disproof of the d>=3 super-Liouvillean small-potential ac question is claimed. The published persistence and counterexample literature was used only to locate the exact quantifier gap, via extraction that may lose equations. Finite-time Lyapunov values and exact resonance bounds are verification-critical supporting evidence only, not substitutes for a spectral proof, and the truncated one-dimensional numerics do not model the full three-frequency operator.
